pictures.c: Isobaths of the base of Quaternary deposits in the Mercure Basin (data: GEMINA [1963]). Paleo-rivers are shown in violet. The present depocenter is located over 5 km to the W of the paleo-depocenter (from De Martini [1996]).

pictures.t: Map of lake deposits of Mercure basin.
pictures.c: Structural and geomorphological analysis of upper Pleistocene lacustrine sediments filling the Mercure basin (from De Martini [1996]).

Geomorphological map of the Mercure Basin; notice that the dashed lines(symbol 2) represent major tectonic lineaments and that landslide-prone areas are marked with symbols 8 to 11 (from Lazzari [1989]).
Tectonic and structural evolution of the Mercure Basin according to Marra [1998]: a transtensional phase (a) is followed by transpression (b).
Structural/morphological map of Mercure Basin. Notice that only faults marked 9 and 10 are considered active, respectively since Villafranchian and Rissian (from Bousquet and Gueremy [1968]).

Drainage pattern of the Mercure Basin; the drainage divide is marked in black. Major stream rotations towards the present depocenter (thick blue line) are marked with red dashed boxes (from De Martini [1996]).

pictures.t: Tectonic setting of the Mercure Basin area
pictures.c: Map showing a) the tectonic setting of the Mercure Basin area; and b) the tectonic lineament as derived from air photo interpretation respect to outcrops of recent continental deposits (from Brozzetti et al. [2009]).
Relocalized 1998 Mercure earthquake sequence and focal mechanisms of larger events mapped on the pattern of recent faults (from Brozzetti et al. [2009]).

pictures.t: Cross sections across the 1998 Mercure earthquake sequence
pictures.c: NNE-SSW trending cross-sections showing relocalized 1998 Mercure earthquake sequence and its relationships with surface faults (from Brozzetti et al. [2009]).

pictures.t: Scheme of the 1998 earthquake seismogenic source
pictures.c: Scheme showing geometry of the hypothesized Piana Perretti seismogenic Fault and relationships with the associated earthquake sequence. The Castelluccio-Rotonda Fault falls in the hanging-wall of the Piana Perretti Fault (from Brozzetti et al. [2009]).
